results.reason: Issue 2 quotes § 14.2, notes the 100% stock sale triggers it, and cites the 30-day termination right. It explains that Schedule 4.4 says 'None', so the § 7.2(c) condition does not capture the consent.

The response cites § 16.1 only for the point that the Customer cannot assign without Supplier consent. It never identifies that Vantrell can assign freely without the Company's consent, and never raises the risk of the contract passing to a competitor or other undesirable party.

Issue 1 calculates the 120-day deadline as September 2, 2026 and notes the SPA was dated September 21, nineteen days later. It states the Extension Pricing right is lost unless notice was already given.

Issue 3 quotes Side Letter § 2 limiting Fundamental Reps to solely 4.1 and 4.2 and explains that § 11.11 gives the Side Letter priority. Its table shows Capitalization and Taxes becoming subject to the deductible and the 10% cap.
Issue 4 contrasts Delaware law and the Court of Chancery with SPA §§ 11.8–11.9 (New York). It notes the Side Letter controls via § 11.11 and that this produces a split forum.
The response states the cap is 10% of the Purchase Price ($8,450,000).
The response states that § 11.11 gives the Side Letter first priority over the SPA.
The response is a memorandum addressed to [Partner]. Each issue lists the documents and sections, a 'why this matters to Halvorsen' discussion, and a recommended fix.
The memo opens with an 'Issues Requiring Immediate Client Call' section and puts the deal-critical issues first.

The response says the deadline has likely passed. Issue 16 mentions a not-yet-passed window only as a hypothetical and calls it the less likely scenario, so it never states the option remains exercisable.
The response states the Side Letter controls and that Capitalization and Taxes become subject to the cap. It does not claim they remain uncapped or that the SPA controls.
